title: Concord Retail POC — Architecture Briefing and Decision Notes
content:
Purpose and audience:
This note is a compact architecture briefing to guide the Concord (large retail) POC decision: pick an initial deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, or private), call out configuration options, and enumerate tradeoffs for the customer workshop on 2024-12-09. Audience: Solutions Eng, Platform Eng, Customer Architecture, Concord SREs, Security.
content_2:
Customer context (short):
- Concord is a multi-region e‑commerce platform with strict PCI adjacency controls and a mix of public product data + sensitive internal pricing and inventory signals.
- Goal for POC: demonstrate a cart-assist feature driven by an ensemble of an open LLM for suggestions + a proprietary reranker. Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for interactive UX. Throughput: spikes up to 800 RPS during promo windows.
- Data residency requirement: customer data must remain in EU for EU traffic.
- Procurement timeline: 6–9 months to finalize contract if POC succeeds.
content_3:
Primary success criteria for POC:
- Functional: accurate end-to-end pipeline (client -> Redwood inference -> re-ranker -> client) with sample prompts and deterministic evaluation harness.
- Performance: meet p95 latency target during baseline traffic (100 RPS) and maintain graceful degradation at 800 RPS.
- Security/compliance: demonstration of encryption-at-rest for model artifacts and request logs, and proof of KMS integration for private deployment option.
- Observability: traceable per-request token cost and latency breakdown in Console dashboards.
- Cost signal: rough cost-per-1000-req estimate for hosted vs dedicated setups.
content_4:
Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not onboard a brand-new model architecture for the POC (use Redwood-verified open model family).
- No production SLA required for POC; limited test data only.
- Concord will not run on-prem hardware for the POC (private deployment will be VPC-hosted or air-gapped optional later).
content_5:
Deployment option summaries (engineer-friendly):
1) Hosted API (fastest path)
   - What: run on Redwood multi-tenant control plane and serving fleet; easiest onboarding, minimal infra for customer.
   - Pros: quickest to demo; no infra ops for Concord; autoscaling for bursts; integrated console for metrics.
   - Cons: data-in-transit to Redwood regions; limited KMS control; potential cost-per-token higher than dedicated at scale.
   - Key config we propose for POC: dedicated model pin (stable version), regional routing to eu-west host, prefix caching enabled, KV cache warmup scripts.
   - When to pick: need fastest time-to-value, low onboarding friction, or Concord declines private infra.
content_6:
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
   - What: reserved GPU pool for Concord within Redwood infra, isolated capacity and stronger throughput/latency predictability.
   - Pros: predictable latency, lower unit cost at higher throughput, supports canary rollouts and custom autoscale policies.
   - Cons: commitment required for capacity, provisioning lead time (~2–4 weeks for capacity reservation), still not customer-managed network.
   - Key config for POC: one small dedicated cluster (8xA100-sim) with autoscale headroom, custom batching profile for 16-token avg, persistent KV caches, shadow re-ranker runs to validate regression.
   - When to pick: Concord expects higher sustained RPS and wants better economics without full private deployment.
content_7:
3) Private (VPC / customer-hosted control plane)
   - What: Redwood control plane optional; compute running in Concord VPC or air-gapped environment with optional on-prem. Full network isolation and KMS/HSM integration.
   - Pros: strongest security posture (data never leaves customer network if fully private), full KMS/HSM control, easier for regulated audits.
   - Cons: longer setup (2–8 weeks + infra approvals), requires Concord infra effort, operator responsibilities on their side or professional services engagement.
   - Key config for POC: pilot in Concord EU VPC using 2–3 G4dn nodes (or equivalent) for cost containment, deploy minimal Redwood runtime container images, enable offline model artifacts via pre-signed artifact bundles.
   - When to pick: required by compliance or strong data residency policies, or for long-term enterprise contract.
content_8:
Tradeoffs matrix (quick bullets):
- Time to first demo: Hosted < Dedicated < Private
- Peak latency safety: Private ~ Dedicated < Hosted (depends on routing)
- Unit cost at scale: Private ≈ Dedicated < Hosted
- Operational burden (customer): Private > Dedicated > Hosted
- Security control: Private > Dedicated > Hosted
- Network complexity: Private (VPC peering, egress) > Dedicated (VPC endpoints) > Hosted (standard TLS)
content_9:
Recommended POC approach (opinionated):
Start Hosted with gated config that mimics private constraints (regional EU tenancy + KMS-backed logging via customer-managed key if possible) and a parallel Dedicated pilot in week 3 if baseline throughput tests indicate sustained >200 RPS. Rationale: fast demo to align product and Concord stakeholders, then pivot to dedicated to validate economics and stable latency for promo loads. Private only if Concord compliance/legal signaled a blocker early in the workshop.
content_10:
POC architecture draft (hosted-first + dedicated fallback):
- Ingress: client app -> Concord API gateway -> Redwood hosted endpoint (eu-west)
- Redwood: pinned model v1.3 (Llama-family variant), prefix KV caching, batching profile tuned to 8ms target scheduling window.
- Re-ranker: run as a separate service in Concord staging (callable via internal API); a shadow rerank pass runs on a mirrored stream for validation.
- Telemetry: Redwood Console captures token-level costs, latency histogram, failed requests. Traces exported to Concord jaeger endpoint via OTLP where allowed.
- Security: TLS mutual where supported; redact PII at client-side; minimal request logs retained for POC (7 days).
- Fallback: when latency > 350ms or error rate >1% fallback to smaller quantized model (compatible variant) with lower token budget.
content_11:
Measurements, tests, and instrumentation plan:
- Synthetic load: run k6 script with traffic shape: baseline 100 RPS, ramp to 800 RPS over 5 minutes, sustained 10 minutes.
- Latency budget tracking: p50/p95/p99, tail latency heatmap by token length.
- Warm cache scenario vs cold start scenario: run separate runs to show delta.
- Quality regression: eval suite of 200 sampled prompts; baseline metrics (RR@1, MRR) for reranker.
- Cost smoke test: estimate tokens/req * cost-per-token for hosted and unit GPU-hour for dedicated (run cost model spreadsheet).
content_12:
Initial cost back-of-envelope (POC scale):
- Hosted: sign-up + demo traffic (100 RPS, 1M tokens/day) ≈ $5k–$8k/month (includes model cost + data transfer)
- Dedicated pilot (small cluster, reserved with burst): monthlyized ≈ $12k–$18k/month (depends on node types and utilization)
- Private pilot (customer infra): infra-only incremental cost (VMs + network egress) ≈ $6k–$10k/month + Redwood private licensing/prof svc one-time fees.
Notes: these are rough, we need infra SKU details from procurement to tighten numbers.
content_13:
Operations checklist for workshop/demo:
- Pre-work (owner: Aisha): obtain sample dataset (anonymized) and access matrix for Concord staging.
- Infra (owner: Liam): provision eu-west hosted endpoint with model pinned; configure logging to use customer KMS if allowed.
- Reranker (owner: Marisol): containerize reranker, validate handshake and latency under shadow mode.
- Load tests (owner: Ethan): prepare k6 scripts and runbook for smoke and blast tests; capture traces.
- Compliance (owner: Riya): prepare answers for encryption-at-rest, retention, data deletion policy.
- Customer ops: schedule workshop agenda, invite Concord security + platform architects, prepare a short SLA/cost appendix.
content_14:
Open questions & decision points for workshop:
- Can Concord accept a hosted demo that routes EU traffic to Redwood eu-west region under a data processing agreement? (Legal)
- Does Concord require private KMS/HSM for request logs or is customer-managed key in Redwood acceptable? (Security)
- What are the expected average token lengths per request during promo bursts? Need sample traces to size batching window. (Product)
- If we choose dedicated, what is the target utilization threshold where dedicated becomes cheaper than hosted for Concord (finance to compute)?
- Is Concord willing to run a minimal set of nodes in their VPC for private pilot, or do they expect Redwood to provision in customer cloud?
content_15:
Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: promo spike causes queuing and latency SLO misses. Mitigation: pre-warm dedicated cluster or set burst capacity; enable autoscaling with conservative headroom.
- Risk: compliance/legal blocks hosted demo. Mitigation: prepare private pilot plan and bring in Legal to draft DPA addendum quickly.
- Risk: reranker integration latency dominates. Mitigation: run reranker in same VPC/region or use colocated instance; profile and optimize early.
content_16:
Proposed timeline (3 week rapid POC):
Week 0 (pre-work until 2024-12-06): collect data, sign basic NDAs, agree on test scenarios.
Week 1 (2024-12-09 workshop): run hosted demo, capture baseline metrics, identify blockers.
Week 2: run scale tests and (if indicated) spin up dedicated pilot.
Week 3: finalize results, produce brief cost/ops readout and recommendation for next-stage procurement.
content_17:
Decisions recorded during syncs:
- 2024-11-27: agreed hosted-first approach for demo (Aisha, Concord PM)
- 2024-12-02: customer asked for KMS option — we will prototype customer-managed key for logs (Riya)
- 2024-12-04: plan to measure reranker latency separately and expose traces in Console (Marisol)
